8	# Feature Specification: FEAT-003 — LLM Providers
9	
10	**Feature ID**: FEAT-003
11	**Status**: Draft
12	**Priority**: P0
13	**Owner**: Fizeau Team
14	
15	## Overview
16	
17	The provider surface is what backs PRD pillar #3 (make local models a real
18	option): one shared abstraction across cloud frontier providers and local
19	serving runtimes, so callers and benchmarks treat them uniformly.
20	
21	Fizeau reaches models through concrete provider systems. Provider identity
22	names the actual source of model service (`lmstudio`, `openrouter`,
23	`anthropic`, `ollama`, `vllm`, `omlx`, and so on), not the wire protocol. The
24	OpenAI-compatible request/streaming shape is a shared SDK layer used by several
25	providers, but it is not a provider identity and must not appear in routing,
26	billing, telemetry, or cost reports.
27	
28	Provider data feeds the routing engine in three ways:
29	
30	- transport and auth: where requests go and how they authenticate;
31	- live signals: model discovery, health, limits, quota, utilization, and cost;
32	- policy defaults: billing classification and `include_by_default`.
33	
34	ADR-009 makes provider billing and default inclusion part of the v0.11 routing
35	contract. Pay-per-token providers are default-deny for unpinned automatic
36	routing unless the provider is included by default and explicit metered-spend
37	opt-in allows them.
38	
39	## Problem Statement
40	
41	- Provider configs historically mixed transport details with routing policy.
42	- OpenAI-compatible local and cloud systems shared request code but needed
43	  different billing, auth, model discovery, and telemetry identity.
44	- Automatic routing must avoid accidental paid API spend while still allowing
45	  explicit pins and opt-in paid routing.
46	
47	## Requirements
48	
49	### Provider Interface
50	
51	1. Providers implement the internal synchronous chat contract used by the core
52	   loop: messages in, tools/options in, response with content/tool calls/token
53	   usage/model/cost metadata out.
54	2. Streaming remains opt-in through the streaming provider interface; the core
55	   loop detects it at runtime.
56	3. Provider packages own provider-specific request shaping, auth defaults,
57	   endpoint defaults, model discovery, limit discovery, cost attribution, quota
58	   discovery, and utilization discovery.
59	4. Shared protocol helpers may exist, but they must not own provider identity,
60	   billing, URL heuristics, or routing decisions.
61	
62	### Concrete Provider Systems
63	
64	5. Supported provider `type` values include `lmstudio`, `omlx`, `ollama`,
65	   `vllm`, `rapid-mlx`, `llama-server`, `lucebox`, `openai`, `openrouter`,
66	   `anthropic`, `google`, and `virtual`.
67	6. `type: openai-compat` is rejected at config load. URL inference may map
68	   known local ports or hosts to concrete provider systems, but only during
69	   config normalization.
70	7. Local providers may expose endpoint pools. Endpoint names are operational
71	   identity for status, logs, sticky routing, and explicit endpoint selection;
72	   they are not the primary routing policy surface.
73	8. Cloud providers may use `base_url` as a single-endpoint override when that
74	   provider supports it.
75	
76	Example:
77	
78	```yaml
79	providers:
80	  studio:
81	    type: lmstudio
82	    include_by_default: true
83	    endpoints:
84	      - name: vidar
85	        base_url: http://vidar:1234/v1
86	      - name: eitri
87	        base_url: http://eitri:1234/v1
88	
89	  openrouter:
90	    type: openrouter
91	    api_key: ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}
92	    include_by_default: false
93	```
94	
95	### Billing Classification
96	
97	9. Billing is a first-class provider attribute with these values:
98	
99	| Billing | Provider systems |
100	|---------|------------------|
101	| `fixed` | `lmstudio`, `llama-server`, `omlx`, `vllm`, `rapid-mlx`, `ollama`, `lucebox` |
102	| `per_token` | `openai`, `openrouter`, `anthropic`, `google` |
103	| `subscription` | built-in account harnesses `claude`, `codex`, `gemini` |
104	| unknown (`""`) | custom or unrecognized systems until config or manifest supplies billing |
105	
106	10. The known provider-system rows are hardcoded through
107	    `BillingForProviderSystem`. Built-in account harnesses use the matching
108	    harness billing table.
109	11. Unknown provider systems must supply an explicit billing value before they
110	    can participate in policy routing. This avoids treating an unknown paid API
111	    as free or local by accident.
112	
113	### Default Inclusion
114	
115	12. `include_by_default` controls whether a provider participates in unpinned
116	    automatic routing.
117	13. Pay-per-token providers default to `include_by_default: false`.
118	14. Fixed/local providers and subscription/account harnesses may be included by
119	    default when the catalog or effective user config says so.
120	15. User config may override the catalog default for a provider.
121	16. Pay-per-token providers additionally require explicit metered-spend opt-in
122	    before they can participate in unpinned automatic routing. Provider default
123	    inclusion is necessary but not sufficient.
124	17. Explicit pins (`Provider`, `Harness`, or exact `Model`) override
125	    `include_by_default`, so an operator can deliberately use a provider that
126	    is excluded from unpinned automatic routing.
127	18. Explicit pins also override metered opt-in, so a deliberately pinned
128	    pay-per-token provider or exact model can be considered without enabling
129	    pay-per-token providers for automatic routing.
130	19. Pins do not override policy `Require` constraints. For example,
131	    `Policy=air-gapped` requires `no_remote`; pinning `openrouter` under that
132	    policy fails with a policy requirement error.
133	
134	### Runtime Identity
135	
136	20. Attempt metadata and public inventory distinguish:
137	
138	```go
139	type AttemptMetadata struct {
140	    Provider string
141	    ProviderType string
142	    ProviderEndpoint string
143	    Model string
144	    CostUSD float64
145	}
146	```
147	
148	21. `Provider` is the configured provider name. `ProviderType` is the provider
149	    system. `ProviderEndpoint` is the endpoint name or normalized host identity
150	    when applicable.
151	22. No code emits the shared protocol name as a provider identity.
152	
153	### Limits and Discovery
154	
155	23. `LookupModelLimits` resolves context window and output-token limits by:
156	    explicit config, then provider-specific live probe, then zero/unknown.
157	24. Provider-specific probes include:
158	    - `lmstudio`: native model metadata for loaded context length;
159	    - `omlx`: `/v1/models/status`;
160	    - `openrouter`: OpenRouter model metadata;
161	    - other providers: zero/unknown unless they expose a verified limit API.
162	25. Live model discovery wins over configured model hints. Configured default
163	    models are fallback hints, not the whole inventory.
164	
165	### Utilization and Health
166	
167	26. Local OpenAI-compatible providers may expose endpoint utilization. The
168	    configured `base_url` remains the API base; probes derive the server root
169	    when needed.
170	27. `vllm`, `rapid-mlx`, `llama-server`, and `omlx` normalize active/queued
171	    work, cache pressure where available, and freshness into provider-neutral
172	    utilization signals.
173	28. Utilization probe failure does not make an endpoint unavailable by itself.
174	    It produces stale/unknown utilization and routing falls back to service-owned
175	    in-flight lease counts plus normal health state.
176	29. LM Studio's chat stats may provide performance counters, but cache pressure
177	    remains unknown unless a verified native counter is available.
178	
179	### Reasoning and Sampling
180	
181	30. `reasoning` is the only public model-reasoning control in provider config,
182	    CLI execution, service requests, and embedding callers.
183	31. Provider-specific terminology such as thinking, effort, variant, and token
184	    budgets remains adapter terminology.
185	32. Sampling defaults remain catalog policy per ADR-007. Routing policies do
186	    not replace sampling profiles; the two surfaces are independent.
187	
188	## Acceptance Criteria
189	
190	| ID | Criterion | Suggested Verification |
191	|----|-----------|------------------------|
192	| AC-FEAT-003-01 | Provider configs accept concrete provider systems and reject `openai-compat` as a provider identity. | `go test ./internal/config ./...` |
193	| AC-FEAT-003-02 | Provider inventory and attempt metadata report configured provider name, provider system, endpoint identity, model, billing, and default-inclusion state. | `go test ./... -run 'ListProviders|AttemptMetadata|ProviderInfo'` |
194	| AC-FEAT-003-03 | `BillingForProviderSystem` classifies fixed, per-token, and unknown provider systems according to the table above; built-in account harnesses classify as subscription. | `go test ./internal/modelcatalog ./... -run Billing` |
195	| AC-FEAT-003-04 | Pay-per-token providers are excluded from unpinned automatic routing unless provider default inclusion and metered opt-in both allow them, while explicit pins can still select them. | `go test ./internal/routing ./... -run 'Policy|IncludeByDefault|Metered|Pin'` |
196	| AC-FEAT-003-05 | Policy requirements still beat pins: a remote provider pinned under `air-gapped` / `no_remote` fails with `ErrPolicyRequirementUnsatisfied`. | `go test ./internal/routing ./... -run Policy` |
197	| AC-FEAT-003-06 | Provider limit and utilization probes preserve unknown/stale states instead of guessing or marking endpoints unavailable solely because utilization failed. | `go test ./internal/provider ./...` |
198	
199	## Constraints and Assumptions
200	
201	- Billing classification is intentionally conservative; unknown means unknown.
202	- Local/fixed billing does not mean zero operating cost in cost reports unless
203	  pricing is reported or explicitly configured.
204	- Ordinary request execution does not fetch remote catalog manifests.
205	- Endpoint labels are operational diagnostics, not policy names.
206	
207	## Dependencies
208	
209	- `FEAT-004` for routing-policy interpretation of provider metadata.
210	- `FEAT-005` for cost and usage projection.
211	- `ADR-009` for the v0.11 routing surface.
212	
213	## Out of Scope
214	
215	- Managing local model downloads or server processes.
216	- Automatic paid-provider opt-in.
217	- Reintroducing provider route tables or user-authored fallback chains.

17	
18	// ScoredModel is a discovered model with a selection preference score.
19	// Higher scores are preferred by the auto-selection logic.
20	type ScoredModel struct {
21		// ID is the model identifier returned by the server's /v1/models endpoint.
22		ID string
23		// CatalogRef is the catalog target ID if this model is recognized in the
24		// model catalog for the provider's surface. Empty for unrecognized models.
25		CatalogRef string
26		// PatternMatch is true when this model matched the configured model_pattern.
27		PatternMatch bool
28		// Score summarises the selection preference: 3 = catalog-recognized,
29		// 2 = pattern-matched, 1 = uncategorized.
30		Score int
31	}
32	
33	// DiscoverModels queries the generic /v1/models endpoint through the shared
34	// OpenAI-compatible SDK. It is kept here as a package-level compatibility
35	// wrapper for existing provider tests and callers inside this package.
36	func DiscoverModels(ctx context.Context, baseURL, apiKey string) ([]string, error) {
37		return openaicompat.DiscoverModels(ctx, baseURL, apiKey)
38	}
39	
40	// RankModels scores and sorts a list of discovered model IDs by selection
41	// preference:
42	//
43	//   - Score 3 — catalog-recognized: the model ID appears in knownModels (a map
44	//     from concrete model ID to catalog target ID, e.g. from
45	//     Catalog.AllConcreteModels). These are explicitly tracked models; prefer
46	//     them when auto-selecting.
47	//   - Score 2 — pattern-matched: the model ID matches the case-insensitive
48	//     pattern regex (pattern == "" means this tier is skipped).
49	//   - Score 1 — uncategorized: known to the server but not in the catalog or
50	//     pattern.
51	//
52	// Within each score tier, the original server-returned order is preserved.
53	// Returns an error only if pattern is non-empty and fails to compile.
54	func RankModels(candidates []string, knownModels map[string]string, pattern string) ([]ScoredModel, error) {
55		var patternRe *regexp.Regexp
56		if pattern != "" {
57			re, err := regexp.Compile("(?i)" + pattern)
58			if err != nil {
59				return nil, fmt.Errorf("discovery: invalid model_pattern %q: %w", pattern, err)
60			}
61			patternRe = re
62		}
63	
64		scored := make([]ScoredModel, 0, len(candidates))
65		for _, id := range candidates {
66			sm := ScoredModel{ID: id, Score: 1}
67			if ref, ok := knownModels[id]; ok {
68				sm.CatalogRef = ref
69				sm.Score = 3
70			} else if patternRe != nil && patternRe.MatchString(id) {
71				sm.PatternMatch = true
72				sm.Score = 2
73			}
74			scored = append(scored, sm)
75		}
76	
77		// Stable sort: higher score first, original order preserved within tier.
78		sort.SliceStable(scored, func(i, j int) bool {
79			return scored[i].Score > scored[j].Score
80		})
81		return scored, nil
82	}
83	
84	// SelectModel picks the preferred model ID from a ranked list. Returns ""
85	// if the list is empty.
86	func SelectModel(ranked []ScoredModel) string {
87		if len(ranked) == 0 {
88			return ""
89		}
90		return ranked[0].ID
91	}
92	
93	// getAndDecode performs a GET request with optional Bearer auth and extra
94	// headers, decodes the JSON response into out, and returns any error.
95	func getAndDecode(ctx context.Context, timeout time.Duration, endpoint, apiKey string, headers map[string]string, out any) error {
96		reqCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
97		defer cancel()
98	
99		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(reqCtx, http.MethodGet, endpoint, nil)
100		if err != nil {
101			return err
102		}
103		req.Header.Set("Accept", "application/json")
104		if apiKey != "" {
105			req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+apiKey)
106		}
107		for k, v := range headers {
108			req.Header.Set(k, v)
109		}
110	
111		resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
112		if err != nil {
113			return err
114		}
115		defer resp.Body.Close() //nolint:errcheck
116	
117		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
118			body, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 256))
119			return fmt.Errorf("HTTP %d: %s", resp.StatusCode, strings.TrimSpace(string(body)))
120		}
121		return json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(out)
122	}
123	
124	// MatchModelIDs returns every catalog entry whose normalized form contains
125	// the normalized request as a substring. Normalization lowercases, strips a
126	// single leading vendor namespace, and removes all non-alphanumeric
127	// separators, so "qwen/qwen3.6" and "Qwen3.6" and "qwen3.6" all match
128	// "Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit" and "Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-nvfp4".
129	//
130	// The returned slice preserves original catalog case and order. An empty slice
131	// means no match; callers are responsible for deciding whether to pass the
132	// original request through to the provider unchanged or to escalate.
133	//
134	// This is the primary matching primitive since v0.9.2 — it replaces the
135	// scalar logic previously in NormalizeModelID. NormalizeModelID is retained
136	// as a backward-compatible wrapper.
137	func MatchModelIDs(requested string, catalog []string) []string {
138		return modelmatch.Match(requested, catalog)
139	}
140	
141	// NormalizeModelID resolves a caller-supplied model name against the server's
142	// canonical model catalog (the IDs returned by GET /v1/models).
143	//
144	// Prefer MatchModelIDs for new code; this wrapper is retained for backward
145	// compatibility with the v0.9.1 call signature. Behaviour:
146	//   - 0 matches → returns the original requested string, no error
147	//   - 1 match   → returns the catalog entry, no error
148	//   - 2+ matches → returns "" and an ambiguity error listing the candidates
149	func NormalizeModelID(requested string, catalog []string) (string, error) {
150		if strings.TrimSpace(requested) == "" {
151			return requested, nil
152		}
153		matches := MatchModelIDs(requested, catalog)
154		switch len(matches) {
155		case 0:
156			return requested, nil
157		case 1:
158			return matches[0], nil
159		default:
160			return "", fmt.Errorf("ambiguous model %q: matches %v", requested, matches)
161		}
162	}

324				name:      "empty request returns empty",

328			},
329			{

392	// lmStudioServer returns an httptest server that serves /api/v0/models/{model}
393	// with the given loaded and max context lengths.
394	func lmStudioServer(loaded, max int) *httptest.Server {
395		return httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
396			if !strings.HasPrefix(r.URL.Path, "/api/v0/models/") {
397				http.NotFound(w, r)
398				return
399			}
400			w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
401			_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(map[string]interface{}{
402				"id":                    strings.TrimPrefix(r.URL.Path, "/api/v0/models/"),
403				"loaded_context_length": loaded,
404				"max_context_length":    max,
405			})
406		}))
407	}
